1.explanation:
1. We define a custom CSS file (`secondary-tabs.css`) that targets the Carbon Tabs’ BEM classes under a new selector `.bx--tabs--secondary`.
2. We override `.bx--tabs__nav-item` to give each tab a gray container, border, and rounded top corners, removing the default underline.
3. The selected state (`.bx--tabs__nav-item--selected`) switches the background to white and hides its bottom border so it merges with the content pane.
4. We tune the link color to gray by default and blue on hover or selection to match the screenshot.
5. In `App.js`, we import Carbon’s Tabs, Tab, and TabContent, include the CSS override, and add `className="bx--tabs--secondary"` on the `<Tabs>` element to activate the custom “secondary” style.  This reproduces the layout and visual styling shown in the bug report image.
1.bug_scenario: The supplied screenshot demonstrates a custom “secondary” styled Tabs component.  Instead of the default blue underline and link‐style tabs, each tab is rendered inside a light gray rounded container with its own border.  The active tab is white with a matching bottom border to blend with the content area, while its label text turns blue on hover or when selected.
